verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core design stores everything as plain-text Markdown files locally, works fully offline without any vendor server (obsidian-docs-20, obsidian-docs-23, obsidian-docs-2), and supports syncing via self-managed channels like Git or third-party storage (obsidian-docs-19) rather than requiring the vendor's Sync service; community evidence confirms a self-hosted sync plugin (Self-Hosted LiveSync) is commonly used specifically to avoid third-party/vendor sync (obsidian-comm-12), and a real-time collaboration plugin was built to fill sync gaps (obsidian-comm-9). Missing for 10: an official first-party self-hosted sync backend (only community plugins fill this role) and independent verification of long-term reliability of those self-hosted options.
